analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia (30 October 2026)
key_insights: US indices closed mostly lower on Thursday: S&P 500 -0.30%, Dow -0.25%, Nasdaq -1.38%, Russell 2000 +1.01%. Breadth was strong, with S&P 500 gainers outnumbering decliners four to one and the equal-weight index beating the cap-weighted index by about 150 bp.

The AI trade weakened as semiconductors and memory gave back part of their large weekly gains and neoclouds fell. Alphabet was the main Magnificent 7 drag, and Microsoft could not hold early gains as its $25B bonding plan drew scrutiny.
Treasury yields fell 3-8 bp after Wednesday's bearish steepening, the dollar index fell 0.2% and WTI settled 0.8% lower.

Q3 GDP first read was +3.4% vs +3.2% consensus, September core PCE +0.3% m/m in line, and initial jobless claims 194K vs 199K forecast. Analysts still largely expect a December Fed hike after Wednesday's hold.

Software and cybersecurity lagged on earnings: ServiceNow -27.0% on a softer cRPO guide (the company and some analysts called it largely accounting/timing), Fortinet -20.1% on an underwhelming beat and raise, Alphabet -12.6% on Search deceleration.

Alphabet Search grew +12% vs +17% in Q2 and +15% consensus, with the company citing FX, tough comps, softer retail and media spending and lower monetization of AI Mode queries. Google Cloud accelerated to +103% from +82%, operating margin expanded about 1,250 bp to 36.2%, and backlog reached $561B with about 55% expected to convert within 24 months.

Microsoft Azure grew +48% in constant currency vs about +45% consensus, with guidance for +49-50% in the Dec Q. Commercial RPO rose 73% to $677B and Copilot daily users rose nearly 50% q/q. Cautious points were slower M365 seat growth, an 11% decline in commercial bookings, no updated Copilot seat count, and capex set to accelerate in 2H.
Pharma/biotech, restaurants, banks, payments and homebuilders outperformed. Glaukos +33.7%, Crocs +25.5% (third guidance raise), Eli Lilly +6.6% on Mounjaro and Zepbound sales ahead of consensus.
Marvell fell 13.2% on a Bloomberg report that it is in talks to acquire Lumentum, with a deal possibly announced this week.

Iran diplomacy: VP Vance sent a letter to Iranian security chief Rezaei to set up a framework for peace negotiations, and Qatar-led mediators are pushing for a deal letting UN nuclear inspectors into Iran. Sticking points are Iran's demand that the US lift its naval blockade and allow oil sales, and the US demand that Iran restart nuclear talks first. Oil was choppy on expectations of renewed military action after the midterms.

FOMC held rates Wednesday as expected. Warsh's press conference suggested an every-other-meeting cadence for potential further hikes, and BofA suggested the lack of a dissent from hawkish Logan may mean she is comfortable with that pace. Warsh plans only seven policy votes next year, with one meeting turned into a strategy session. Consensus for a December hike is little changed.

European equities rose: DAX +1.5%, CAC +1.1%, FTSE 100 +0.3%. The market rewarded guidance raises and capital returns and sold misses and cautious outlooks even on modest headline beats. Bund 2 bp lower at 3.36%, gilts 5 bp lower at 5.29%.

The ECB held rates as expected and said financing conditions have tightened since September, which is likely to weigh on inflation and growth. Consensus expects another ECB hike in December. The ECB also confirmed Lagarde will step down on 7-Feb, earlier than her October 2027 term end, with de Cos the favorite per a Bloomberg economist survey and Knot also named.
Eurozone ESI fell to 96.9 from 97.5 vs 97.7 consensus, the second straight decline and weakest since June, with energy prices linked to the Iran conflict weighing on consumers and businesses.

Eurozone October flash HICP (4-Nov) is expected to edge up to about 3.9% y/y from 3.8%, with core near 2.5% and energy HICP about 20% y/y. Goldman Sachs sees core peaking at 2.7% in Q1 2027, ABN Amro and MUFG see headline above 4%, and Commerzbank sees headline not declining until spring 2027.

UK Chancellor Healey deferred big fiscal decisions in a lowkey Budget with a muted bond reaction. Sell-side estimates put the fiscal gap at at least £25B, and next year's Spending Review becomes more important.

Asia was mixed: Nikkei +1.10%, Hang Seng -0.59%, Shanghai Composite -0.82%, Kospi -1.24%. Advantest's results lifted Kioxia and Tokyo Electron in Japan, while Samsung Electronics fell 4.1% as Q3 net profit (KRW75T) missed the KRW86.1T consensus and no new shareholder return plan was announced.
Samsung guided that the chip shortage will likely deepen next year, expects double-digit percent foundry revenue growth in Q4, and sees capex rising almost 60% to KRW84.4T vs KRW74.4T consensus.

SK Hynix Q3 operating profit of KRW83.3T beat the KRW77.5T consensus on a +20% q/q ASP increase. It expects the memory supply gap to last through 2030, has LTAs with 14 customers covering more than 50% of 2027-2028 capacity, and plans a KRW20T buyback plus a KRW14T dividend.

Chinese tech sold off again: ChiNext -4.5%, STAR 50 -4.3%, both heading for six straight weekly losses. STAR 50 is down nearly 20% MTD and trades at about 38x forward earnings vs under 5x for the Kospi.

BOJ decision due Friday: consensus expects no change, with the Outlook Report expected to say underlying inflation has effectively reached 2%, which would support a December hike. The BOJ's neutral rate range estimate is 1.1-2.5%, with consensus terminal rate near 1.75%.

Japan faces a second wave of food price hikes as Middle East turmoil lifts naphtha and tanker costs. Middle East-to-Asia shipping rates are nearly six times pre-Hormuz-closure levels, a record, and pass-through to consumers typically takes about six months.

market_movers.rationale: Stock +33.7% on Q3 revenue and EPS beat, strong Epioxa sales, raised FY26 revenue guidance and a ~$1B preliminary 2027 revenue outlook, about 17% above consensus.
Stock +25.5% on a Q3 beat and third raise of FY26 guidance. HEYDUDE returned to growth.
Stock +15.7% on Q3 EBITDA and revenue beat and FY26 EBITDA guided to the high end of range. Analysts disliked higher SG&A per unit.
Stock +15.1% on Q3 revenue beat with Brinsupri ahead of consensus and raised FY26 Brinsupri and Arikayce guidance.
Stock +6.6% on Q3 beat, Mounjaro and Zepbound sales ahead of consensus and raised FY revenue and margin guidance.
Stock +5.6% after confirming the acquisition of CART at $65.00 per share, EV about $17B, closing end of 2027 or 1H28. Q3 orders were 993M, up 28% y/y.
Stock +5.5% on fiscal Q1 beat, raised 2026 WFE outlook to the mid-$150B range and a >$200B 2027 WFE outlook.
Stock -12.6% on softer Search growth despite Google Cloud +103%.
Azure accelerated to +48% cc and was guided to +49-50%, but the stock could not hold early gains as the $25B bonding plan drew scrutiny.
Stock -13.2% on a Bloomberg report of talks to acquire Lumentum, deal possible as soon as this week.
Stock -20.1% as the beat and raise underwhelmed, with sharp product revenue deceleration and a services revenue miss.
Stock -27.0% on softer cRPO guidance despite a Q3 beat and raised FY26 subscription revenue, FCF margin and AI ACV guidance.
Stock -9.3% as FY26 guidance was reaffirmed, not raised, and backlog growth slowed sequentially.
Stock -22.6% on Q3 comps down 0.9% and Q4 guidance with EPS about 60% below the Street.
Stock +1.6% to a record high after Q3 net income of $10.8B and a quarterly buyback raised to $5B.
Stock +8.8% on Q3 comps +2.1% vs +1.5% consensus and positive traffic. Margin pressure is the focus.
Stock +3.8% on Q3 EPS and revenue beat, though about $550M of revenue upside was purchase timing.

sector_views.rationale: ServiceNow, Fortinet and SAP fell on soft guidance and renewed concern that AI could disrupt application-software economics, even after beats and raises.
US semis gave back large weekly gains, while SK Hynix and Samsung point to a memory shortage lasting years and Advantest and KLA raised outlooks.
Sector outperformed in the US on earnings beats and raised guidance from Lilly, Merck, Insmed and Glaukos.
STAR 50 and ChiNext fell sharply on valuation concerns, with STAR 50 at about 38x forward earnings.

earnings_insights: Alphabet Q3 (reported 10/29): Search +12% vs +17% in Q2 and +15% consensus. Google Cloud +103% vs +82% prior quarter. Operating margin 36.2%, backlog $561B.
Microsoft fiscal Q1 (reported): Azure +48% constant currency vs about +45% consensus, Dec Q guide +49-50%. Commercial RPO +73% to $677B.
ServiceNow Q3 (reported): beat and raised FY26 subscription revenue, FCF margin and AI ACV guidance. Stock fell 27.0% on softer cRPO guidance.
Fortinet Q3 (reported): KPIs mostly better and FY26 guide raised, but product revenue growth decelerated sharply and services revenue missed.
Eli Lilly Q3 (reported): earnings, revenue and gross margin beat. Mounjaro and Zepbound ahead of consensus, FY revenue and margin guidance raised.
Caterpillar Q3 (reported): earnings better, revenue in line, FY26 guidance reaffirmed.
Samsung Electronics Q3 (reported): operating profit KRW107T in line with preliminary, net profit KRW75T vs KRW86.1T consensus, semiconductor profit KRW106.5T vs KRW108.5T consensus.
SK Hynix Q3 (reported): operating profit KRW83.3T vs KRW77.5T consensus, revenue KRW104.6T vs KRW99T consensus.
Shell Q3 (reported): net income $10.8B beat expectations, buyback raised to $5B, 2026 capex guidance lowered to $23-25B.
Lloyds Q3 (reported): revenue missed expectations by 1%, with net interest margin and CET1 below forecasts.
Haleon Q3 (reported): organic growth 2.6% vs 3.4% consensus, FY26 sales growth guidance cut to about 2.5%.
Chipotle Q3 (reported): comps +2.1% vs +1.5% consensus, traffic +0.8%, Q4 comps guided to about +2%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Beat the 3.2% consensus and Q2's +2.2%, helped by consumer spending and investment.
In line with consensus. August was revised up to +0.3% from +0.2%, and annualized core is +3.1%.
Below the 199K forecast. Continuing claims were 1701K vs 1720K consensus.
Slightly below the +0.6% consensus, with income +0.2% vs +0.3%.
Analysts still largely expect a December hike, with Warsh suggesting an every-other-meeting cadence.
Consensus is for another hike in December as financing conditions have tightened.
Down from 97.5 vs 97.7 consensus, the weakest since June.
Consensus is for a rise from 3.8% in September, with core near 2.5%.
The Outlook Report is expected to say underlying inflation has reached 2%, supporting a December hike.
Oil choppy on Iran diplomacy headlines vs expectations of post-midterm military action.

risk_factors: Software earnings reactions show investors penalizing even beat-and-raise reports on guidance details, and AI disruption concerns for application software.
Alphabet Search deceleration and lower AI Mode monetization.
Microsoft capex acceleration in 2H, slower M365 seat growth, and the $25B bonding plan.
Further Fed hikes in December and an every-other-meeting hike cadence.
Renewed US military action against Iran after the midterms and the Hormuz closure's effect on energy prices.
Eurozone inflation near 4% by year-end, with tighter financing conditions weighing on growth.
UK fiscal gap of at least £25B with unclear consolidation plans.
China tech valuation correction (STAR 50 at about 38x forward earnings) and questions on whether earnings support valuations.
Possible change in ECB leadership with Lagarde leaving on 7-Feb.
vol_and_positioning: Volatility index at 17.20, up 1.71% on the day.
US breadth was very positive: S&P 500 gainers outnumbered decliners four to one, and equal-weight outperformed cap-weighted by about 150 bp.
STAR 50 down nearly 20% MTD to its lowest since Sep-25, heading for six straight weekly losses.
geopolitical: US-Iran diplomacy: VP Vance letter to Iranian security chief Rezaei, Qatar-led mediation on UN inspector access, and a US naval blockade as a sticking point.
Expectation of renewed US military action against Iran after the midterms.
Middle East conflict and the Strait of Hormuz closure raising energy, freight and food costs in Europe and Japan.
Czech Dukovany nuclear contract talks reportedly collapsed for the KHNP and Daewoo E&C consortium.
Deutsche Telekom halted merger plans with T-Mobile US due to works council pushback.
cross_bank_references: BofA suggested the lack of a dissent from hawkish Logan may mean she is comfortable with the every-other-meeting hike pacing.
Goldman Sachs sees Eurozone core inflation peaking at 2.7% in Q1 2027.
ABN Amro and MUFG see Eurozone headline inflation moving above 4% in coming months.
Commerzbank sees Eurozone headline inflation not declining until spring 2027.
ING noted the Eurozone economy has shown relative resilience, with PMIs indicating continued expansion.
Capital Economics noted sentiment is consistent with at-trend quarterly GDP growth of about 0.3%.
